findings.title: Unshared sovereignty and concluding praise
findings.claim: The wider echoes let the focus's three negations read together as one account of unshared sovereignty: child-taking, a co-sharer in dominion, and an ally required by lowliness are each denied; praise and takbir voice the resulting independence. Their recurrence elsewhere makes the final command an affirmation of that sovereignty, not an isolated intensifier.
findings.mechanism: The focus carriers yattakhidh/waladan, sharik fi al-mulk, wali min al-dhull, al-hamdu lillah, and kabbirhu/takbira meet distinct supplied surface echoes. 25:2 repeats child-taking and no partner in dominion; 23:91 places no child and no co-deity beside the consequence of rival creators; 34:22 denies a share and a supporter; 2:107 pairs Allah's dominion with creatures having no guardian or helper besides Him; 31:26 joins possession, self-sufficiency, and praise; 45:37 places kibriya across the heavens and earth; and 74:3 repeats the magnification command. Fatiha 1:2 returns the opening al-hamdu lillah through the focus's closing praise. Together these contacts change the three negatives from separate denials into a linked account of unassisted rule, answered by praise and declared greatness. The further contrast with prayer volume in 17:110 is retained only as the attributed reading of the legacy reader walk.
findings.reader_payoff: The ending returns to Fatiha's opening praise while moving from denied lineage, divided rule, and compensatory support to an affirmative command to magnify. The final greatness can be read as structural and doxological, not merely acoustic, with the acoustic contrast explicitly qualified.
findings.containment: The focus's ordinary child/offspring sense remains primary; the creation wording in 23:91 does not make walad mean generic creation. Wider connections are assessed from supplied Arabic surface wording only because target morphology and lexical analysis are absent; no direct borrowing, shared occasion, or inherited connection ranking is claimed. The 17:110 volume distinction is attributed to legacy_unbound support, not established here as a lexical fact or as the whole meaning of takbir.

epistemic.reason: A trusted focus-linked synthesis and exact supplied Arabic surface parallels support the integrated reading, while target-side morphology is missing and the 17:110 acoustic distinction depends on legacy_unbound attribution.

branch_activations.facet_statement: Bir şeyi kendisi için edinip kendine ait hale getirmeyi anlatır.
branch_activations.carrier: The focus's jussive yattakhidh with waladan denotes taking or adopting a child for oneself.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: The supplied wording of 25:2 repeats child-taking beside the denial of a partner in dominion and the statement that all things are created and measured.
branch_activations.activation: The repeated child-taking denial is paired with exclusive dominion in 25:2, returning the focus's taking verb and object to a wider sovereignty formula.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The opening denial functions as the first member of a linked statement of non-derivative and undivided rule.
branch_activations.boundary: This does not make walad mean generic creation or establish direct literary borrowing; offspring remains the ordinary focus sense.

branch_activations.branch_gloss: yermenin karşıtı olan, iyilik için teşekkürü de kapsayan övgü
branch_activations.carrier: The focus's definite al-hamdu is praise in the closing formula al-hamdu lillah.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: Fatiha 1:2 supplies the same opening al-hamdu lillah formula; 31:26 places the surface wording of possession alongside al-ghani and al-hamid.
branch_activations.activation: The identical Fatiha praise formula returns through the focus's al-hamdu, while 31:26 couples praise with possession and self-sufficiency; this links the closing praise to the independence just denied in the focus.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The focus's hamd is heard as praise affirming unassisted sovereignty and as a return to the recitation's opening praise.
branch_activations.boundary: The target-side morphology of 31:26 is not supplied; the claim rests on its visible wording and the direct al-hamdu lillah repetition in 1:2.

branch_activations.branch_gloss: bir şeyden nedenle türeme veya sonradan oluşturulma
branch_activations.facet_statement: Belirli söz biriminde bir şey, başka bir şeyden bir neden aracılığıyla ortaya çıkar.
branch_activations.carrier: The focus denies taking a walad, ordinarily an offspring or child, into relation with God.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: 23:91 places the denial of a child beside the imagined division in which each rival deity would take what it created.
branch_activations.activation: The contrast between offspring and what rival creators bring about touches the derivative relation carried by the focus's child denial and distinguishes it from created things in the wider formula.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The denial also participates in a wider contrast between divine independence and derivative creation, without changing the ordinary meaning of walad.
branch_activations.boundary: This is a contextual contrast, not a claim that walad itself means any created object or that 23:91 supplies the focus word's morphology.

branch_activations.facet_statement: Bir şey, hak veya iş en az iki taraf arasında ortaktır ve taraflardan yalnız birine ait değildir.
branch_activations.carrier: The focus's sharik names a co-sharer, specifically one in al-mulk.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: 25:2 repeats the denial of a partner in dominion; 23:91 denies a deity alongside God and imagines the consequence of rival creators claiming ascendancy over one another.
branch_activations.activation: The repeated no-partner wording and the consequence of competing deities return to the focus's sharik fi al-mulk as a denial of divided rule, not merely a generic social partnership.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The co-sharer negation becomes the rule-bearing middle of the focus's linked independence sequence.
branch_activations.boundary: No target-side morphology is inferred, and the focus does not name a human political arrangement.

branch_activations.facet_statement: Bir kişi, mal veya hak üzerinde sahiplikten doğan elinde bulundurma ve tasarruf yetkisine sahiptir.
branch_activations.carrier: Al-mulk is the sovereignty or possession in which the focus denies a partner.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: 34:22's supplied wording denies the alleged deities ownership even of an atom and denies them a share in the heavens and earth.
branch_activations.activation: The explicit no-ownership/no-share wording returns to the focus's al-mulk and sharpens the denied partnership as a question of possession and disposition.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The focus's no-partner clause is heard as excluding both shared title and shared authority.
branch_activations.boundary: The target's exact Arabic is supplied but its morphology and lexical analysis are not; the parallel is limited to its transparent ownership/share wording.

branch_activations.facet_statement: Hükümdar, halk üzerinde emir ve yasak koyarak kamusal yönetim yetkisi kullanır.
branch_activations.carrier: The focus places the denied sharik within al-mulk, the domain of rule and dominion.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: 25:2's supplied wording gives God the dominion of the heavens and earth and then denies child and partner in that dominion.
branch_activations.activation: The wider pairing of cosmic dominion with no partner returns to the focus's al-mulk and connects the word to unshared public sovereignty.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The focus's partner denial concerns divided authority as well as possession.
branch_activations.boundary: The human-ruler core is activated only as the general rule-authority facet; no human political institution is being described in the focus.

branch_activations.facet_statement: İlahi bağlamda bütün varlık üzerindeki mutlak ve kalıcı egemenlik anlatılır.
branch_activations.carrier: The focus's al-mulk names the dominion in which no partner is admitted.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: 25:2 explicitly places dominion of the heavens and earth with God and couples it with the denial of a child and partner.
branch_activations.activation: The divine cosmic scope in 25:2 returns to the focus's al-mulk and activates the branch's divine-sovereignty specialization; the core facet is retained above.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The no-partner clause reads as exclusive, comprehensive sovereignty rather than a limited share in a human realm.
branch_activations.boundary: This is a bounded divine-context specialization; the connection does not supply target-side morphology or prove a direct citation.

branch_activations.facet_statement: Sevgi, dostluk, inanç veya yardım bağıyla birinin yanında yer alma.
branch_activations.carrier: The focus's wali is a close ally or supporter, denied as something needed because of lowliness.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: 34:22 says the alleged deities are no supporter for God; 2:107 pairs Allah's dominion with creatures having no wali or helper besides Allah.
branch_activations.activation: The first wording echoes the absent-support relation, while the second reverses its direction: creatures lack protection apart from Allah. Both return through the focus's wali clause.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The denied divine need for a supporter is contrasted with creaturely dependence on Allah, making the focus's independence relational rather than merely a list of absent allies.
branch_activations.boundary: The contrast does not imply that God could need support; target morphology is unavailable and the reversal is limited to the supplied surface wording.

branch_activations.branch_gloss: hor ve güçsüz duruma düşüp boyun eğme
branch_activations.facet_statement: Kişi, saygınlık ve karşı koyma gücü bakımından aşağı bir konuma düşer ve boyun eğer.
branch_activations.carrier: Min al-dhull frames the denied wali as support sought from lowliness or weakness.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: 31:26 places possession and the surface praise term al-hamid alongside al-ghani, the self-sufficient.
branch_activations.activation: The focus's lowliness-based need for a supporter meets the wider pairing of possession with self-sufficiency; the contrast makes the stated absence of a wali follow from divine independence, not from lacking an available ally.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The wali negation is grounded in freedom from need, completing the sequence from no child to no co-ruler to no compensatory support.
branch_activations.boundary: The connection is based on supplied surface wording; no target-side morphology or unprovided theological premise is asserted.

branch_activations.facet_statement: Bir varlık veya değerin küçüğe göre daha büyük ölçü ya da derece taşıması temel anlamdır.
branch_activations.carrier: Kabbirhu is the command to magnify Him, reinforced by the cognate verbal noun takbiran.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: 45:37 places al-kibriya across the heavens and earth; 74:3 supplies the direct command wa-rabbaka fa-kabbir.
branch_activations.activation: Cosmic grandeur in 45:37 and the parallel magnification command in 74:3 return to the focus's k-b-r command and verbal noun, giving the final act a Quranic scale and a direct performative echo.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The ending's magnification declares greatness on a cosmic scale and answers the sovereignty just affirmed.
branch_activations.boundary: The parallels do not establish identical inflection, occasion, or direct literary dependence; the target morphology is not supplied.

branch_activations.facet_statement: Bir varlık veya değerin küçüğe göre daha büyük ölçü ya da derece taşıması temel anlamdır.

branch_activations.independent_trigger: The legacy wide reader walk attributes to 17:110 a calibration away from excessively loud or inaudible prayer and reads that nearby cue against a vocal-only interpretation of the final takbir.
branch_activations.activation: Under that attributed contextual reading, the volume guidance returns to the focus's command to magnify and makes structural greatness, rather than increased sound alone, perceptible.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The final takbir can be read as conceptual and doxological magnification rather than simply raising the voice.
branch_activations.boundary: This is attributed legacy_unbound interpretation, not an independently established lexical restriction or proof that 17:110 exhausts the meaning of the focus.

branch_activations.facet_statement: Bir şeyi zihinde büyük görmek ve önemini olduğundan ya da sıradan düzeyden yüksek değerlendirmek çekirdektir.
branch_activations.carrier: The focus's imperative and cognate verbal noun make magnifying God's greatness an instructed act.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: 45:37 places al-kibriya across the heavens and earth, while 74:3 supplies the parallel command wa-rabbaka fa-kabbir.
branch_activations.activation: The parallel command returns through the focus's kabbirhu/takbiran and supports the evaluative core of regarding God as great, while the cosmic grandeur in 45:37 fixes the scale of that regard.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: Magnification includes an affirmative appraisal of God's greatness, not only an abstract degree or an intensified utterance.
branch_activations.boundary: Only the branch's core regard-as-great facet is retained; spontaneous astonishment is not claimed, and the focus remains an imperative declaration.

branch_activations.facet_statement: Tanrı'yı en büyük ilan eden söz aracılığıyla yüceltme temel eylemdir.
branch_activations.carrier: Kabbirhu and takbiran directly carry the act of magnifying God in the focus.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: The supplied wording of 74:3 says wa-rabbaka fa-kabbir, a direct Quranic magnification command.
branch_activations.activation: The parallel imperative returns to the focus's same magnifying act and activates the specific exaltation branch available under the focus root.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The final takbir is heard as an explicit act of exalting God, not merely as a generic statement that something is large.
branch_activations.boundary: Only the core exaltation facet is activated; the target's morphology and ritual setting are not supplied, so no claim about a fixed formula or identical grammatical form is made.
